claim: RNA-catalyzed RNA replication is widely believed to have supported a primordial biology.
source: RNA-catalyzed RNA replication is widely believed to have supported a primordial biology.
evidence: This is a statement about scientific consensus in the field, presented as established knowledge.

claim: RNA catalysis is dependent upon RNA folding.
source: However, RNA catalysis is dependent upon RNA folding, and this yields structures that can block replication of such RNAs.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about RNA structure-function relationships.

claim: RNA folding yields structures that can block replication of RNAs.
source: However, RNA catalysis is dependent upon RNA folding, and this yields structures that can block replication of such RNAs.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the structure vs. replication paradox.

claim: A general and accurate triplet polymerase ribozyme emerged from in vitro evolution as a mutualistic RNA heterodimer.
source: We report RNA-catalysed RNA synthesis on structured templates when using trinucleotide triphosphates (triplets) as substrates, catalysed by a general and accurate triplet polymerase ribozyme that emerged from in vitro evolution as a mutualistic RNA heterodimer.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from in vitro evolution experiments.

claim: Triplets cooperatively invaded and unraveled even highly stable RNA secondary structures.
source: The triplets cooperatively invaded and unraveled even highly stable RNA secondary structures, and support non-canonical primer-free and bidirectional modes of RNA synthesis and replication.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Triplet substrates support non-canonical primer-free modes of RNA synthesis and replication.
source: The triplets cooperatively invaded and unraveled even highly stable RNA secondary structures, and support non-canonical primer-free and bidirectional modes of RNA synthesis and replication.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Triplet substrates support bidirectional modes of RNA synthesis and replication.
source: The triplets cooperatively invaded and unraveled even highly stable RNA secondary structures, and support non-canonical primer-free and bidirectional modes of RNA synthesis and replication.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The triplet polymerase ribozyme can synthesise its own catalytic subunit '+' and '–' strands in segments.
source: Triplet substrates thus resolve a central incongruity of RNA replication, and here allow the ribozyme to synthesise its own catalytic subunit '+' and '–' strands in segments and assemble them into a new active ribozyme.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The triplet polymerase ribozyme can assemble synthesized segments into a new active ribozyme.
source: Triplet substrates thus resolve a central incongruity of RNA replication, and here allow the ribozyme to synthesise its own catalytic subunit '+' and '–' strands in segments and assemble them into a new active ribozyme.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Some RNA sequences can catalyse and template their own replication by reciprocally synthesizing their own '+' and '–' strands.
source: The premise that some RNA sequences can catalyse and template their own replication - reciprocally synthesizing their own '+' and '–' strands - underpins current thinking about early genetic systems (Crick, 1968; Orgel, 1968; Szostak et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to foundational work in the field.

claim: Any ancient ribozyme with RNA replicase capability seems to be lost.
source: Any ancient ribozyme with such RNA replicase capability seems to be lost, but efforts are ongoing to recreate RNA self-replication in the laboratory (Martin et al., 2015) as a critical test of the 'RNA world' hypothesis (Gilbert, 1986).
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Derivatives of naturally occurring self-splicing introns were shown to be able to assemble one of their own strands from cognate constituent RNA segments.
source: Early on, derivatives of naturally occurring self-splicing introns (Doudna et al., 1991; Green and Szostak, 1992; Hayden and Lehman, 2006) as well as later in vitro evolved ligase ribozymes (Lincoln and Joyce, 2009; Sczepanski and Joyce, 2014) were shown to be able to assemble one of their own strands from cognate constituent RNA segments.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In vitro evolved ligase ribozymes were shown to be able to assemble one of their own strands from cognate constituent RNA segments.
source: Early on, derivatives of naturally occurring self-splicing introns (Doudna et al., 1991; Green and Szostak, 1992; Hayden and Lehman, 2006) as well as later in vitro evolved ligase ribozymes (Lincoln and Joyce, 2009; Sczepanski and Joyce, 2014) were shown to be able to assemble one of their own strands from cognate constituent RNA segments.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ligase ribozyme systems require specific preformed building blocks of at least eight nucleotides average length.
source: However, a critical drawback of such systems is their need for specific preformed building blocks of at least eight nucleotides (nt) average length, limiting their potential for open-ended evolution, and precluding their replication from pools of random-sequence oligonucleotide substrates (Green and Szostak, 1992; Doudna et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: RNA polymerase ribozymes have been developed that can use general monomer building blocks (ribonucleoside 5' triphosphates) in RNA-templated RNA synthesis.
source: In a contrasting approach, RNA polymerase ribozymes (RPRs) have been developed that can use general monomer building blocks (ribonucleoside 5' triphosphates (NTPs)) in RNA-templated RNA synthesis (Johnston et al., 2001; Zaher and Unrau, 2007; Wochner et al., 2011; Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016), akin to the activity of modern proteinaceous polymerases.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Even the most highly-evolved RPRs are substantially impeded by template secondary structures.
source: However, even the most highly-evolved RPRs (Horning and Joyce, 2016) are substantially impeded by template secondary structures.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Template secondary structures are ubiquitous in larger, functional RNAs and generally indispensable for function.
source: Such structures are ubiquitous in larger, functional RNAs (including the RPRs themselves) and generally indispensable for function.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about RNA structure-function relationships.

claim: There is an antagonism between the degree to which an RNA sequence is able to fold into a defined three-dimensional structure to encode function and the ease with which it can be replicated.
source: The strong inhibitory role of this central feature of RNA leads to an antagonism between the degree to which an RNA sequence is able to fold into a defined three-dimensional structure to encode function (such as catalysis) and the ease with which it can be replicated (Boza et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Models of non-enzymatic polymerisation of all four activated ribonucleotides yield pools of di-, tri- and tetranucleotide etc. length oligonucleotides in decreasing abundance dominating the population alongside longer products.
source: Models of non-enzymatic polymerisation of all four activated ribonucleotides – the presumed source of the first RNA sequences – yield pools of di-, tri- and tetranucleotide etc. length oligonucleotides (in decreasing abundance) dominating the population alongside longer products (Monnard et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A truncated version of the Z RPR comprising its catalytic core domain (Zcore) exhibited weak templated ligation activity.
source: However, we detected a weak templated ligation activity in a truncated version of the Z RPR comprising its catalytic core domain (Zcore) (Figure 1a), which supported incorporation of oligonucleotide substrates as short as three nt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) when incubated in the eutectic phase of water ice (Attwater et al., 2010; Mutschler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Zcore supported incorporation of oligonucleotide substrates as short as three nucleotides when incubated in the eutectic phase of water ice.
source: However, we detected a weak templated ligation activity in a truncated version of the Z RPR comprising its catalytic core domain (Zcore) (Figure 1a), which supported incorporation of oligonucleotide substrates as short as three nt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) when incubated in the eutectic phase of water ice (Attwater et al., 2010; Mutschler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: After 7 rounds of in-ice evolution, one-quarter of the selection pool comprised an improved ribozyme (type 0).
source: After 7 rounds of in-ice evolution, one-quarter of the selection pool comprised an improved ribozyme (type 0).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The 0core ribozyme could catalyze the iterative polymerization of multiple triplets.
source: Its core domain (0core, Figure 1a) could catalyse the iterative polymerization of multiple triplets allowing us to begin to investigate the properties of triplet-based RNA replication.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: 0core could catalyze triplet polymerisation on a series of structured templates, which had proven intractable to the parental Z RPR.
source: Significantly, we found that 0core could catalyze triplet polymerisation on a series of structured templates, which had proven intractable to the parental Z RPR (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Primer extension by 0core exhibited a steep sigmoidal dependence upon triplet concentrations.
source: Here, primer extension exhibited a steep sigmoidal dependence upon triplet concentrations (Figure 1c), suggestive of a cooperative invasion and unraveling of template secondary structures by the triplet substrates themselves.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The sigmoidal dependence of primer extension on triplet concentration is suggestive of cooperative invasion and unraveling of template secondary structures by the triplet substrates.
source: Here, primer extension exhibited a steep sigmoidal dependence upon triplet concentrations (Figure 1c), suggestive of a cooperative invasion and unraveling of template secondary structures by the triplet substrates themselves.
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data, representing an inference from the observed sigmoidal relationship.

claim: At round 21, type 1 RNAs comprised approximately 50% of pool sequences.
source: Type 1 RNAs were the most abundant, comprising ~50% of pool sequences, but mysteriously were catalytically inactive with diverse mutations in their core domains.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by sequencing data.

claim: Type 1 RNAs were catalytically inactive with diverse mutations in their core domains.
source: Type 1 RNAs were the most abundant, comprising ~50% of pool sequences, but mysteriously were catalytically inactive with diverse mutations in their core domains.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Type 2–6 RNAs all displayed triplet polymerase activity.
source: In contrast, the type 2–6 RNAs all displayed triplet polymerase activity, but fell short of the polyclonal activity of the selection pool (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Addition of an equimolar amount of type 1 RNA substantially enhanced triplet polymerase activity of all the other ribozyme types 2–6.
source: To attempt to explain this discrepancy, we explored potential interactions among the different pool lineages, and found that addition of an equimolar amount of type 1 RNA substantially enhanced triplet polymerase activity of all the other ribozyme types 2–6 (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: 5' truncation of the region that previously contacted the primer/template duplex in type 1 RNA did not affect its cofactor activity.
source: Dissecting type 1 RNA function, we found that 5' truncation of the region that previously contacted the primer/template duplex (Shechner et al., 2009) did not affect its cofactor activity (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citation.

claim: Type 1 RNA appears to form a 1:1 heterodimeric complex directly with active triplet polymerase ribozymes.
source: As judged by gel mobility shift (Figure 3b) and activity enhancement (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), type 1 RNA appears to form a 1:1 heterodimeric complex directly with active triplet polymerase ribozymes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The 'cap+' hairpin is the critical site of interaction between type 1 and active triplet polymerases.
source: 'cap–' was dispensible for type 1's cofactor activity, but when replacing 'cap+' in active triplet polymerases it abolished both their activity enhancement by type 1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and complex formation (Figure 3b). This points to the 'cap+' hairpin as the critical site of interaction with type 1; 'cap–' in type 1 presumably served to deter its homodimerisation during selection.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and inference.

claim: Type 1 enhancement allows type 5 variants to synthesise long RNAs using triphosphorylated oligonucleotide or short triplet substrates.
source: In complex with type 5 (the fastest enriching triplet polymerase ribozyme in the final selection pool), type 1 boosts polymerization of triplets (or longer oligonucleotides) to enable synthesis of long RNAs (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Type 1 obviates the need for ribozyme-template tethering.
source: Here, it became apparent that type 1 also obviates the need for ribozyme-template tethering.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The triplet polymerase heterodimer appears to have a capacity for true intermolecular, sequence-general interaction with primer-template duplexes.
source: In contrast, the triplet polymerase heterodimer appears to have a capacity for true intermolecular, sequence-general interaction with primer-template duplexes, which enables holoenzyme formation and copying of RNA templates without requiring specific ribozyme-template hybridization sites.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The final t5+1 triplet polymerase heterodimer comprises a 135 nt subunit (1) and a 153 nt subunit (t5).
source: Below, the secondary structure of this ribozyme heterodimer, 135 nt (1) and 153 nt (t5) long, is depicted operating in trans on a non-tethered primer/template duplex.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by structural data shown in Figure 4.

claim: t5+1 robustly copied hairpin-containing templates with estimated TMs of up to 93°C.
source: To provide a stringent test of template structure inhibition, we now examined hairpin-containing templates (4S, 6S, 8S) with increasing RNA hairpin stability and estimated TMs of up to 93˚C (8S). The latter had previously strongly arrested even the most advanced mononucleotide RPRs at higher temperatures (Horning and Joyce, 2016). However, using triplets as substrates t5+1 robustly copied all of these (Figure 5a), even when templates were pre-folded allowing RNA secondary structures to form prior to triplet addition (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures and citation.

claim: The triplet concentration-dependent cooperative structure invasion and unraveling was recapitulated with t5+1 and the highly stable 8S hairpin template.
source: The triplet concentration-dependent cooperative structure invasion and unraveling (previously observed with the simpler 0core domain and partly wobble-paired RNA template structures [Figure 1b,c]) was recapitulated with t5+1 and the highly stable 8S hairpin template (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Dinucleotide triphosphate substrates yielded extension only up to the structured region.
source: In contrast, dinucleotide triphosphate substrates yielded extension only up to the structured region (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: t5+1 could synthesise both a functional fluorescent '+' strand of the 52 nt Broccoli RNA aptamer and its encoding '−' strand template from their constitutive triplets.
source: Encouragingly, t5+1 could synthesise both a functional fluorescent '+' strand of the 52 nt Broccoli RNA aptamer (Filonov et al., 2014) and its encoding '−' strand template from their 13 (+) and 12 (−) different constitutive triplets (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b and citation.

claim: t5+1 achieved synthesis of the β+, γ+, and δ+ segments from their constitutive triplets starting from ~8 nt RNA primers.
source: Starting from ~8 nt RNA primers, t5+1 achieved synthesis of the β+, γ+, and δ+ segments from their constitutive triplets as well as all of the '−' strand segments α-, β-, γ-, δ- and ε-, but required some triplets pre-linked (as e.g. hexa- or nonanucleotides) for synthesis of full-length α+ and ε+ segments (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: t5+1 achieved synthesis of all of the '−' strand segments α-, β-, γ-, δ- and ε- from their constitutive triplets starting from ~8 nt RNA primers.
source: Starting from ~8 nt RNA primers, t5+1 achieved synthesis of the β+, γ+, and δ+ segments from their constitutive triplets as well as all of the '−' strand segments α-, β-, γ-, δ- and ε-, but required some triplets pre-linked (as e.g. hexa- or nonanucleotides) for synthesis of full-length α+ and ε+ segments (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: t5+1 required some triplets pre-linked as hexa- or nonanucleotides for synthesis of full-length α+ and ε+ segments.
source: Starting from ~8 nt RNA primers, t5+1 achieved synthesis of the β+, γ+, and δ+ segments from their constitutive triplets as well as all of the '−' strand segments α-, β-, γ-, δ- and ε-, but required some triplets pre-linked (as e.g. hexa- or nonanucleotides) for synthesis of full-length α+ and ε+ segments (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The average extent of ligation per junction during synthesis of t5 '+' and '−' strands was 78%.
source: Operating across 70 distinct ligation junctions in these reactions including AU-rich sequences, t5+1demonstrates the sequence generality for self-synthesis using triplet substrates. Notably, the average extent of ligation per junction during synthesis of t5 '+' and '−' strands (78%) was similar to that observed when t5+1 used an unstructured model template (74%, Figure 3c) upon which the parental Z and other RPRs excel (Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: t5+1 could assemble synthesised '+' strand segments into αβ+ and γδε+ fragments, guided only by partially overlapping '−' strands.
source: At this point, we tested whether the broad oligonucleotide ligation capacity of t5+1 (Figure 3c) might allow assembly of synthesised '+' strand segments. Indeed, t5+1 could assemble these into αβ+ and γδε+ fragments, guided only by partially overlapping '−' strands (Figure 6b, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The ribozyme-synthesised αβ+ and γδε+ fragments spontaneously reconstituted a new catalytically active triplet polymerase ribozyme through non-covalent association.
source: Through non-covalent association (Vaish et al., 2003; Mutschler et al., 2015), the ribozyme-synthesised αβ+ and γδε+ fragments spontaneously reconstituted a new catalytically active triplet polymerase ribozyme (with in vitro transcribed type 1 RNA).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: The ribozyme-synthesized and assembled triplet polymerase could regenerate fresh δ- segment using t5+1 ribozyme-synthesised δ+ as a template.
source: We found that this synthesis product could regenerate fresh δ- segment using t5+1 ribozyme-synthesised δ+ (left over from ribozyme assembly) as a template (Figure 6c), recapitulating elements of a self-replication cycle.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: More concentrated triplet substrates can successfully compete with ribozyme unstructured elements for hybridization to '−' strand templates.
source: Additionally, more concentrated triplet substrates can successfully compete with ribozyme unstructured elements for hybridization to '−' strand templates (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: t5+1 can extend primers bidirectionally, in both the canonical 5'−3' as well as the reverse 3'−5' directions.
source: Unexpectedly, triplet substrates provide a route to bypass the 'primer problem'. We observed that t5+1 can extend primers bidirectionally, in both the canonical 5'−3' as well as the reverse 3'−5' directions (Figure 7a).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: t5+1 can achieve 'primer free' RNA synthesis.
source: Given this flexibility, we wondered if t5+1 even had a requirement for a primer oligonucleotide. Indeed, this triplet polymerase could achieve 'primer free' RNA synthesis (whereby synthesis is presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template), as exemplified here for the β+ segment (Figure 7b), as well as 'primer free' RNA replication as shown for the '+' and '−' strands of the γ segment, which can be replicated using triplets alone (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Random sequence triplet pools ('pppNNN') could be used as substrates by t5+1 in segment syntheses in place of defined triplet sets.
source: Random sequence triplet pools ('pppNNN', comprising equimolar amounts of all 64 triplets) could be used as substrates by t5+1 in segment syntheses in place of defined triplet sets (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Extension activity remained robust upon pool supplementation with noncanonical dinucleotide and mononucleotide substrates.
source: Furthermore, extension activity remained robust upon pool supplementation with noncanonical dinucleotide and mononucleotide substrates (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claim: The starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited approximately 91% fidelity per position.
source: On average, the starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited ~91% fidelity per position (Figure 8a), lower than that described for RPRs (92% – 97% [Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016]).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a and citations.

claim: Zcore accuracy exhibited a pronounced downward gradient from the first (5') to the third (3') triplet position.
source: Furthermore, its accuracy exhibited a pronounced downward gradient from the first (5') to the third (3') triplet position, highlighting escalating risks to fidelity of synthesis founded on longer building blocks.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The final t5+1 ribozyme achieves an average positional fidelity of 97.4% using pppNNN.
source: Notably, the final t5+1 ribozyme achieves an average positional fidelity of 97.4% using pppNNN in this sequence context, higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable eutectic conditions (Attwater et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citation.

claim: Deep sequencing of internal triplet positions of a defined sequence (β+ segment) synthesised by t5+1 using pppNNN indicated similar aggregate fidelity could be achieved during longer product synthesis excluding the final triplet.
source: Deep sequencing of internal triplet positions of a defined sequence (β+ segment) synthesised by t5+1 using pppNNN indicated similar aggregate fidelity could be achieved during longer product synthesis excluding the final triplet (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: The type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute to fidelity gains.
source: Investigating the fidelity contributions of different t5+1 ribozyme components, we found that the type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute; rather, fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain, as its deletion (yielding the truncated 'αβγδ' ribozyme) reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain.
source: Investigating the fidelity contributions of different t5+1 ribozyme components, we found that the type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute; rather, fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain, as its deletion (yielding the truncated 'αβγδ' ribozyme) reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Presence of the ε domain selectively reduced the most acute errors at the second and third triplet positions.
source: Presence of the ε domain did not uniformly increase fidelity, but selectively reduced the most acute errors at the second and third triplet positions (with over 10-fold reductions for some errors, Figure 8b, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Overall error rates at the second and third triplet positions were reduced by 4-fold and 9-fold compared to Zcore.
source: Overall error rates at the second and third triplet positions were reduced by 4-fold and 9-fold compared to Zcore (Figure 8a), though increased (1.3-fold) at the first triplet position due to a localised asymmetric tolerance of G:U wobble pairing (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The ε domain fidelity function is contingent upon the presence of a downstream triplet.
source: The ε domain fidelity function is contingent upon the presence of a downstream triplet, operating only with basal fidelity for final triplet incorporation (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: Using triplet substrates modified at the third position with a 2-thiouracil in place of a uracil rendered the ε fidelity domain unable to discriminate mismatches.
source: Dissecting the molecular determinants of the fidelity phenotype, we found that using triplet substrates modified at the third position with a 2-thiouracil in place of a uracil (disrupting minor groove hydrogen bonding capabilities) rendered the ε fidelity domain unable to discriminate mismatches (Figure 8c, Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Inclusion of complementary triplets caused a striking (~3 fold) drop in misincorporation errors in some direct pair-mispair triplet contests.
source: We observed that in some direct pair-mispair triplet contests, inclusion of their complementary triplets caused a striking (~3 fold) drop in misincorporation errors (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Raising pppNNN concentrations from 0.5 to 5 μM each almost halved the overall error rate.
source: Indeed, counterintuitively, raising pppNNN concentrations from 0.5 to 5 μM each almost halved the overall error rate (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The fidelity enhancement at higher pppNNN concentrations was driven by pronounced reductions in errors where the mismatched triplet has a high GC content compared to the cognate triplet.
source: Although diverse effects upon individual misincorporations were observed, this fidelity enhancement was driven by pronounced reductions in errors where the mismatched triplet has a high GC content compared to the cognate triplet, including common G-U wobble mispairs (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: More efficient, higher fidelity segment synthesis was observed when using an pppNNN pool formulated with a reduced G content.
source: Indeed, more efficient, higher fidelity segment synthesis was observed when partially mimicking this outcome using an pppNNN pool formulated with a reduced G content (Figure 6—figure supplement 4, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures and table.

claim: The triplet polymerase ribozyme comprises a heterodimer of a catalytic triplet polymerase subunit (t5) and a non-catalytic RNA cofactor (type 1).
source: Here, we describe the discovery and characterization of a ribozyme (t5+1) with a robust ability to polymerize RNA trinucleotide triphosphate (triplet) substrates. Unusually, this triplet polymerase ribozyme comprises a heterodimer of a catalytic triplet polymerase subunit (t5) and a non-catalytic RNA cofactor (type 1), which enhances triplet polymerase activity and abrogates the need for template tethering.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The quaternary structure of the triplet polymerase ribozyme is reminiscent of the processivity factors of some proteinaceous polymerases such as the heterodimeric p66/p51 HIV reverse transcriptase holoenzyme.
source: Such a quaternary structure - involving a heterodimer of a full-length and a truncated subunit - is reminiscent of the processivity factors of some proteinaceous polymerases such as the heterodimeric p66/p51 HIV reverse transcriptase holoenzyme (Huang et al., 1992).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison, supported by citation.

claim: The spontaneous emergence of a general, mutualistic RNA cofactor has not previously been observed for ribozymes.
source: However, the spontaneous emergence of a general, mutualistic RNA cofactor has not previously been observed for ribozymes and may suggest an underappreciated dimension to the evolutionary dynamics of ribozyme pools under stringent adaptive pressures.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding, representing knowledge about the field.

claim: The t5+1 ribozyme's principal current shortcoming is its low catalytic efficiency.
source: The t5+1 ribozyme's principal current shortcoming is its low catalytic efficiency.
evidence: This is an assessment of the ribozyme's performance based on experimental data.

claim: In the optimal context for mononucleotide polymerase ribozymes, the triplet polymerase heterodimer yields approximately 4 fold more unligated junctions than the RPR tC19Z.
source: In the optimal context for mononucleotide polymerase ribozymes, this triplet polymerase heterodimer yields ~4 fold more unligated junctions than the RPR tC19Z (Attwater et al., 2013b), which itself is 240-fold slower than the currently most advanced RPR 24–3 (Horning and Joyce, 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: When binding templates, triplets incur a lower entropic cost per position compared to canonical mononucleotides.
source: For instance, when binding templates, triplets incur a lower entropic cost per position compared to canonical mononucleotides (thus aiding copying of sequences rich in weakly pairing A and U bases), with particularly helpful stability contributions from intra-triplet base stacking (Eigen, 1971).
evidence: This is an inference about the molecular properties of triplets, supported by citation.

claim: Energetically favourable inter-triplet stacking interactions appear to instigate cooperative binding and unfolding of even highly stable RNA template structures upon reaching the required substrate concentration threshold.
source: Furthermore, energetically favourable inter-triplet stacking interactions appear to instigate cooperative binding and unfolding of even highly stable RNA template structures (Figures 1b and 5a) upon reaching the required substrate concentration threshold.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of cooperative binding, supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: A general solution to the copying of structured RNAs arises from conditions that promote base-pairing rather than conditions that disfavour it.
source: Counterintuitively, a general solution to the copying of structured RNAs arises not from conditions that disfavour base-pairing (which would also hinder substrate binding), but rather from conditions that promote it.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental findings about triplet-based RNA synthesis.

claim: A triplet/template duplex presents a more ordered, regular target for sequence-general ribozyme docking than a single stranded template.
source: A triplet/template duplex presents a more ordered, regular target for sequence-general ribozyme docking (by e.g. the ε domain) than a single stranded template (variably prone to secondary structure formation or sequence-specific interactions with the ribozyme [Wochner et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is an inference about the structural basis of ribozyme function, supported by citation.

claim: Mechanistic analogies between the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome are apparent.
source: While phylogenetically unrelated, mechanistic analogies between the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome are apparent. Both are RNA heterodimers that operate in a triplet register along a single-stranded RNA template, whilst enforcing a minor-groove mediated pattern of triplet or anticodon readout (including tolerance of 5' wobble pairing), suggestive of convergent adaptive solutions to the challenges of replication and decoding.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of structural and functional features.

claim: It has long been speculated that the decoding centre of the small ribosomal subunit might have had its origins in an ancestral RNA replicase.
source: It has long been speculated that the decoding centre of the small ribosomal subunit might have had its origins in an ancestral RNA replicase, but the implied triplet-based character of such a replicase was conspicuously discordant with modern mononucleotide-based replication (Weiss and Cherry, 1993; Poole et al., 1998; Noller, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about prior speculation in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The utility of triplets as substrates for RNA synthesis and self-synthesis suggests that early ideas about the ribosome's origins in an RNA replicase deserve to be reconsidered.
source: The utility of triplets as substrates for RNA synthesis and self-synthesis described herein suggests that these early ideas deserve to be reconsidered.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study.

claim: An early reliance upon triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
source: In the context of initial uncorrelated evolution of the small and large ribosomal subunits (Petrov et al., 2015), it is tempting to speculate that an early reliance upon triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study and citation.

claim: Short RNA oligonucleotides may represent predisposed substrates for RNA-catalyzed RNA replication.
source: In conclusion, the unexpected emergent properties of triplets – including cooperative binding and unfolding of structured RNA templates, enhanced incorporation of AU-rich substrates, and error attenuation (resulting from triplet pool interaction networks) – argue that short RNA oligonucleotides may represent predisposed substrates for RNA-catalyzed RNA replication.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claim: Some benefits of triplets might extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation.
source: Some of these benefits might also extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation, and to the non-enzymatic replication of RNA (Szostak, 2012), where downstream trinucleotides have recently been shown to enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides both through stacking and positioning effects (Vogel et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2018) and the formation of a highly reactive intermediate (Prywes et al., 2016; O'Flaherty et al., 2018).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to related work.

claim: The interaction of triplet substrate pools with RNA templates promotes uncoupling of an RNA's sequence from its replicability.
source: Taken together, the interaction of triplet substrate pools with RNA templates promotes uncoupling of an RNA's sequence (i.e. information content, and associated folding tendencies) from its replicability, thereby enhancing RNA's capacity to serve as an informational polymer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of the study.

claim: Z RPR has only a very limited template ligation activity slightly exceeding background nonenzymatic ligation.
source: Z RPR has only a very limited template ligation activity (slightly exceeding background nonenzymatic ligation [Rohatgi et al., 1996]).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and citation.

claim: 3' truncation of Z RPR abolished mononucleotide polymerase activity but accommodated and enhanced templated ligation.
source: In contrast, 3' truncation (which abolished mononucleotide polymerase activity) accommodated and enhanced templated ligation.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The selection strategy required iterative templated triplet ligation by ribozymes to achieve their covalent linkage to a tagged primer.
source: We devised a selection strategy that required iterative templated triplet ligation by ribozymes to achieve their covalent linkage to a tagged primer (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the selection strategy.

claim: Transplanting the conserved 5' 'cap+' sequence from types 2–6 allows the Zcore but not the 0core ribozyme triplet polymerase activity to be enhanced by type 1.
source: Left, transplanting the conserved 5' 'cap+' sequence from types 2–6 allows the Zcore but not the 0core ribozyme triplet polymerase activity to be enhanced by type 1
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: RNA polymerase activity of Z RPR using NTPs is enhanced by type 1 addition, but only when modified with the 5' 'cap+' sequence.
source: Right, RNA polymerase activity of Z RPR using NTPs is enhanced by type 1 addition, but only when modified with the 5' 'cap+' sequence (Z RPRcap+), extending primer A10 on tethered template HTI (0.5 μM of each RNA, 4 mM of each NTP, at 4˚C for 68 hr).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The type 0 ribozyme had gone extinct by round 21 of selection.
source: At this point, the type 0 ribozyme had gone extinct, replaced by six new types of RNA each characterised by a unique 3' domain (Figure 2a, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by sequencing data.

claim: Six new types of RNA (types 1-6) emerged by round 21, each characterised by a unique 3' domain.
source: At this point, the type 0 ribozyme had gone extinct, replaced by six new types of RNA each characterised by a unique 3' domain (Figure 2a, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by sequencing data.

claim: Type 5 was the fastest enriching triplet polymerase ribozyme in the final selection pool.
source: In complex with type 5 (the fastest enriching triplet polymerase ribozyme in the final selection pool), type 1 boosts polymerization of triplets (or longer oligonucleotides) to enable synthesis of long RNAs (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by selection data.

claim: RPRs generally depend upon tethering to template due to their poor affinity for primer/template duplex.
source: Due to their poor affinity for primer/template duplex (Lawrence and Bartel, 2003), RPRs generally depend upon such tethering to template (Attwater et al., 2010; Wochner et al., 2011; Horning and Joyce, 2016), which enhances local ribozyme concentration and promotes formation of the RPR-primer/template holoenzyme (Attwater et al., 2010; Attwater et al., 2013a).
evidence: This is established knowledge about RPRs supported by citations.

claim: The 8S hairpin template had previously strongly arrested even the most advanced mononucleotide RPRs at higher temperatures.
source: The latter had previously strongly arrested even the most advanced mononucleotide RPRs at higher temperatures (Horning and Joyce, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Synthesis by the Z RPR is completely arrested by the 6S and 8S hairpins.
source: While all hairpin templates are robustly copied by t5+1, synthesis by the Z RPR is completely arrested by the 6S and 8S hairpins.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The Broccoli aptamer is a fluorescent RNA aptamer.
source: Encouragingly, t5+1 could synthesise both a functional fluorescent '+' strand of the 52 nt Broccoli RNA aptamer (Filonov et al., 2014) and its encoding '−' strand template from their 13 (+) and 12 (−) different constitutive triplets (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The catalytic t5 ribozyme was divided into five segments α, β, γ, δ and ε.
source: As t5+1 currently lacks the efficiency to synthesise RNAs its own length, we divided the catalytic t5 ribozyme into five segments α, β, γ, δ and ε.
evidence: This describes the experimental strategy used in the study.

claim: Segmentation strategy could reduce tertiary structures and ease product separation during RNA replication.
source: This segmentation strategy (akin to that used by some RNA viruses e.g. influenza) could reduce tertiary structures (Doudna et al., 1991; Mutschler et al., 2015) and ease product separation during RNA replication (Szostak, 2012).
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of segmentation, supported by citations.

claim: The geometric mean of the final extents of ligation across all 70 junctions in the self-synthesis context was 78%.
source: Densitometry gave yields of full-length products (boxed, by % of total primer), and a geometric mean of the final extents of ligation across all 70 junctions in this self-synthesis context (78%).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The ribozyme-synthesized and assembled αβ+/γδε+ ribozyme is as active as in vitro transcribed equivalents.
source: The ribozyme-synthesized and assembled αβ+/γδε+ ribozyme is as active as in vitro transcribed equivalents, and can efficiently utilize ribozyme-synthesized RNA (δ+) as a template.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly will need to be increased significantly to realise a full self-replication cycle.
source: However, while the t5+1 ribozyme displays a nascent capacity for templated synthesis of its own catalytic domain '+' strands (and '−' strands), efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly will need to be increased significantly to realise a full self-replication cycle (which would also require synthesis and replication of the type 1 subunit).
evidence: This is an assessment of current limitations and future requirements.

claim: A full self-replication cycle would require synthesis and replication of the type 1 subunit.
source: However, while the t5+1 ribozyme displays a nascent capacity for templated synthesis of its own catalytic domain '+' strands (and '−' strands), efficiency of both segment synthesis and assembly will need to be increased significantly to realise a full self-replication cycle (which would also require synthesis and replication of the type 1 subunit).
evidence: This is an inference about requirements for full self-replication.

claim: Some specific oligonucleotide substrates were required for efficient synthesis of α+ and ε+ segments to compete out inhibitory mutual hybridisation between '−' strand template and corresponding '+' strand unstructured elements in the t5 ribozyme.
source: In particular, some specific oligonucleotide substrates were required for efficient synthesis of α+ and ε+ segments to compete out inhibitory mutual hybridisation between '−' strand template and corresponding '+' strand unstructured elements in the t5 ribozyme (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: In vitro selections that stabilise the ribozyme tertiary structure may contribute to attenuating the requirement for specific oligonucleotide substrates.
source: In vitro selections that stabilise the ribozyme tertiary structure (Figure 6—figure supplement 3) may contribute to attenuating this requirement.
evidence: This is speculation about future improvements, supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: All RPRs require primers to initiate syntheses, akin to the activity of replicative polymerases in biology.
source: The majority of specific oligonucleotides, however, were provided as primers to initiate syntheses, as required by all RPRs akin to the activity of replicative polymerases in biology.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RPRs and biological polymerases.

claim: The priming sequence would effectively be excluded from evolution during replication.
source: As a consequence of this, the priming sequence would effectively be excluded from evolution during replication.
evidence: This is an inference about the consequences of primer-dependent replication.

claim: RNA oligonucleotides able to act as specific primers are unlikely to be prevalent in prebiotic substrate pools.
source: Furthermore, RNA oligonucleotides able to act as specific primers are unlikely to be prevalent in prebiotic substrate pools, and their depletion during successive replication cycles could lead to loss of sequence at genome ends.
evidence: This is speculation about prebiotic chemistry.

claim: The 'primer problem' has previously been noted in the context of nonenzymatic replication as one of the fundamental obstacles to RNA self-replication.
source: This 'primer problem' has previously been noted in the context of nonenzymatic replication (Szostak, 2012) as one of the fundamental obstacles to RNA self-replication.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Bidirectional extension allows not only completion of RNA synthesis from either template end but also initiation from anywhere along a template.
source: This allows not only completion of RNA synthesis from either template end but also initiation from anywhere along a template, potentially allowing non-classical hierarchical or distributive RNA replication schemes as previously proposed (Szostak, 2011).
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of bidirectional extension, supported by citation.

claim: Primer-free RNA synthesis is presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template.
source: Indeed, this triplet polymerase could achieve 'primer free' RNA synthesis (whereby synthesis is presumably initiated by ligation of adjacent triplets anywhere on the template), as exemplified here for the β+ segment (Figure 7b), as well as 'primer free' RNA replication as shown for the '+' and '−' strands of the γ segment, which can be replicated using triplets alone (Figure 7c).
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of primer-free synthesis.

claim: A ribozyme operating in a more distributive polymerisation mode might be able to replicate RNA sequences directly from pools of short random RNA oligonucleotides furnished by prebiotic chemistry.
source: Such a ribozyme operating in a more distributive polymerisation mode might be able to replicate RNA sequences directly from the putative pools of short random RNA oligonucleotides furnished by prebiotic chemistry.
evidence: This is speculation about potential prebiotic applications.

claim: A replicase must incorporate the correct template-complementary substrate from random sequence pools, or genetic information may become irretrievably corrupted during replication.
source: However, a replicase must incorporate the correct template-complementary substrate from random sequence pools, or genetic information may become irretrievably corrupted during replication (Eigen, 1971).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based RNA replication by the need to discriminate between 64 distinct substrates.
source: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based RNA replication by the need to discriminate between 64 distinct substrates; indeed, a previous investigation into the incorporation of individual trinucleotides indicated that misincorporations could outstrip cognate incorporation for some triplets (Doudna et al., 1993).
evidence: This is an inference about the fidelity challenge, supported by citation.

claim: A previous investigation indicated that misincorporations could outstrip cognate incorporation for some triplets.
source: The fidelity challenge is exacerbated in triplet-based RNA replication by the need to discriminate between 64 distinct substrates; indeed, a previous investigation into the incorporation of individual trinucleotides indicated that misincorporations could outstrip cognate incorporation for some triplets (Doudna et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Zcore fidelity is lower than that described for RPRs (92% – 97%).
source: On average, the starting Zcore ribozyme exhibited ~91% fidelity per position (Figure 8a), lower than that described for RPRs (92% – 97% [Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016]).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: t5+1 fidelity is higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable eutectic conditions.
source: Notably, the final t5+1 ribozyme achieves an average positional fidelity of 97.4% using pppNNN in this sequence context, higher than the best RPR fidelity with NTPs under comparable eutectic conditions (Attwater et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citation.

claim: Deletion of the ε domain reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore.
source: Investigating the fidelity contributions of different t5+1 ribozyme components, we found that the type 1 RNA cofactor did not contribute; rather, fidelity gains appeared to be mediated by the newly-evolved t5 'ε' 3'-domain, as its deletion (yielding the truncated 'αβγδ' ribozyme) reverted the fidelity profile towards that of Zcore (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Error rates at the first triplet position increased 1.3-fold due to a localised asymmetric tolerance of G:U wobble pairing.
source: Overall error rates at the second and third triplet positions were reduced by 4-fold and 9-fold compared to Zcore (Figure 8a), though increased (1.3-fold) at the first triplet position due to a localised asymmetric tolerance of G:U wobble pairing (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: A similar replacement of a uracil 2-keto group with a 2-thio modification had been shown to impair Z RPR activity when present upstream in the primer/template region.
source: Previously, a similar replacement of a uracil 2-keto group with a 2-thio modification had been shown to impair Z RPR activity when present upstream in the primer/template region (Attwater et al., 2013a), where Z is thought to rely upon sequence-general minor groove contacts through an 'A-minor' motif (Shechner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Z is thought to rely upon sequence-general minor groove contacts through an 'A-minor' motif.
source: Previously, a similar replacement of a uracil 2-keto group with a 2-thio modification had been shown to impair Z RPR activity when present upstream in the primer/template region (Attwater et al., 2013a), where Z is thought to rely upon sequence-general minor groove contacts through an 'A-minor' motif (Shechner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Modification at the third triplet position reverts ε's divergent effects on fidelity at the adjacent second and the distal first triplet positions.
source: Modification at the third triplet position reverts ε's divergent effects on fidelity at the adjacent second and the distal first triplet positions (Figure 8—figure supplement 3); disruption of this minor groove contact site thus abolishes overall ε fidelity domain operation.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: ε sensitivity to minor groove composition may be critical to its recognition of cognate Watson-Crick base pairs.
source: ε sensitivity to minor groove composition may be critical to its recognition of cognate Watson-Crick base pairs, reminiscent of Tetrahymena group I intron folding (Battle and Doudna, 2002) and the decoding centre of the ribosome (which also tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous (5') triplet position) (Ogle et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of fidelity, supported by citations.

claim: The decoding centre of the ribosome tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous (5') triplet position.
source: ε sensitivity to minor groove composition may be critical to its recognition of cognate Watson-Crick base pairs, reminiscent of Tetrahymena group I intron folding (Battle and Doudna, 2002) and the decoding centre of the ribosome (which also tolerates wobble pairing at the analogous (5') triplet position) (Ogle et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Differential formation of triplet:anti-triplet dimers in the reaction may explain the drop in misincorporation errors upon inclusion of complementary triplets.
source: A potential explanation may arise from differential formation of triplet:anti-triplet dimers in the reaction: for example, more extensive pppGCC:pppGGC (than pppACC:pppGGU) dimer formation would selectively reduce the effective concentration of free pppGCC vs. pppACC upon inclusion of their complementary pppGGC and pppGGU.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of fidelity enhancement.

claim: Dimer formation among pppNNN substrate pools would be expected to selectively buffer the free concentrations of the more strongly-pairing GC-rich triplets.
source: Dimer formation among pppNNN substrate pools would be expected to selectively buffer the free concentrations of the more strongly-pairing GC-rich triplets, which could promote both fidelity and sequence generality through normalization of triplet availability against template (and complementary triplet) binding strength.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of fidelity enhancement.

claim: The potential for replication to proceed in different triplet registers may provide a degree of resilience towards biases in substrate pool composition.
source: However, the potential for replication to proceed in different triplet registers may provide a degree of resilience towards such biases.
evidence: This is speculation about the robustness of triplet-based replication.

claim: There are multiple examples of dimerization in RNA evolution.
source: There are multiple examples of dimerization in RNA evolution - such as the VS ribozyme (Suslov et al., 2015), retroviral RNA genome dimerization (Paillart et al., 2004), in vitro evolved heterodimeric RNA liposome binders (Vlassov et al., 2001), and recently the homodimeric CORN fluorescent RNA aptamer (Warner et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The extinction of previously dominant species in the selection that were unable to benefit from type 1 enhancement illustrates the potential for symbioses to shape RNA molecular ecologies.
source: Indeed, the extinction of previously dominant species in the selection that were unable to benefit from type 1 enhancement (e.g. type 0, see Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and succession with cooperative RNA species (Vaidya et al., 2012) illustrates the potential for such symbioses to shape RNA molecular ecologies.
evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary dynamics, supported by data and citation.

claim: Despite modest catalytic power, t5+1 displays much enhanced generality in RNA synthesis.
source: Yet despite this modest catalytic power, t5+1 displays much enhanced generality in RNA synthesis and now achieves both copying of previously intractable structured RNA templates, and templated synthesis and assembly of an active '+' strand copy of its catalytic domain, suggesting key contributions of the triplet substrates themselves.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the study.

claim: The process of cooperative binding and unfolding is aided by the cold temperature and solute concentration effects of eutectic ice phase formation.
source: In our work, this process is aided by the cold temperature and solute concentration effects of eutectic ice phase formation (Attwater et al., 2010; Mutschler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by citations.

claim: General duplex interactions underlie other notable features observed in triplet-based RNA synthesis such as in trans template binding.
source: Such general duplex interactions also underlie other notable features observed in our triplet-based RNA synthesis such as in trans template binding (Figure 3c) as well as the capacity for bidirectional (5'−3'/3'−5') and primer-free RNA synthesis (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an inference about the structural basis of observed features, supported by data.

claim: RNA-catalyzed triplet polymerisation can proceed with a fidelity matching or exceeding even the best mononucleotide RNA polymerase ribozymes.
source: Contrary to expectations RNA-catalyzed triplet polymerisation can proceed with a fidelity matching or exceeding even the best mononucleotide RNA polymerase ribozymes (Attwater et al., 2013b; Horning and Joyce, 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: t5+1 ribozyme fidelity is due to both a readout of cognate minor groove interactions by the ribozyme ε domain and an unanticipated fidelity boost arising from systems-level properties of triplet pools.
source: t5+1 ribozyme fidelity is due to both a readout of cognate minor groove interactions by the ribozyme ε domain (Figure 8) and an unanticipated fidelity boost arising from systems-level properties of triplet pools, that appear to normalize the availability of free triplet (and potentially longer oligonucleotide) substrates against their base-pairing strength (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the study supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Triplet pool properties likely involve formation of cognate or near-cognate triplet:anti-triplet interaction networks.
source: Though further work will be required to characterize triplet pool properties, they likely involve formation of cognate or near-cognate triplet:anti-triplet interaction networks, as formation of tRNA dimers via cognate anticodon:anticodon interactions has been observed in a similar concentration range (Eisinger and Gross, 1975).
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism, supported by citation to analogous observations.

claim: Both the triplet polymerase ribozyme and the ribosome are RNA heterodimers that operate in a triplet register along a single-stranded RNA template.
source: Both are RNA heterodimers that operate in a triplet register along a single-stranded RNA template, whilst enforcing a minor-groove mediated pattern of triplet or anticodon readout (including tolerance of 5' wobble pairing), suggestive of convergent adaptive solutions to the challenges of replication and decoding.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of structural and functional features.

evidence: This is a statement about prior speculation in the field, supported by citations.

source: In the context of initial uncorrelated evolution of the small and large ribosomal subunits (Petrov et al., 2015), it is tempting to speculate that an early reliance upon triplets in RNA replication could have inadvertently supplied a decoding center for translation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

source: Some of these benefits might also extend to codon/anticodon dynamics in early translation, and to the non-enzymatic replication of RNA (Szostak, 2012), where downstream trinucleotides have recently been shown to enhance incorporation of preceding activated mononucleotides both through stacking and positioning effects (Vogel et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2018) and the formation of a highly reactive intermediate (Prywes et al., 2016; O'Flaherty et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent work.
